tldr: MPP adds a Payment authentication scheme to HTTP 402. The server sends a challenge, the client pays through a named method and retries with a credential, and the server returns a receipt.
whyItExists: An agent that wants one API call, one page of data or a stream of model tokens should not need an account, an API key and a card on file first. MPP puts the price and the proof of payment into the ordinary HTTP authentication headers, so a client can pay on the first request. Because the core says nothing about money movement, the same challenge and credential shape works for stablecoins on Tempo and other chains, Stripe Shared Payment Tokens, Visa network tokens and Lightning, and each rail writes its own method.

whatItIsNot.text: Not Stripe-only. Tempo Labs and Stripe co-author the core, and Visa, Lightspark, Circle, Coinbase and others author payment methods.
Not an IETF standard. The core is an individual Internet-Draft with no working group, no stream and no intended status, and IANA has registered none of its names.
Not crypto-only. Methods cover cards through Stripe Shared Payment Tokens and Visa network tokens, plus Bitcoin over Lightning.
Not the MPP of AP2. In AP2 documents, MPP means Merchant Payment Processor, an unrelated role.
Not a standardized session intent. Only charge and subscription are in specs/intents; session is defined inside method specs, and the generic session pull request closed unmerged on 2026-09-28.
Not x402. The two are separate HTTP 402 designs with a documented mapping, and the mppx SDK can serve both on one route.
Not an identity or mandate protocol. The core has no agent identity and no user authorization object; identity is an optional SDK add-on.

changedRecently.text: draft-httpauth-payment-00 appeared on the IETF Datatracker under a new name while draft-ryan-httpauth-payment-01 was still active.
Tempo session v2, on a TIP-20 channel reserve precompile, merged into the session spec (blog post 2026-06-17).
The subscription intent merged with Stripe and Tempo subscription methods.
The header challenge parameter and the Payment-Authorization field merged, so a credential can travel next to a bearer token.
mppx 0.9.0 added dual MPP and x402 wrappers for Express, Hono, Next.js and MCP.
XRPL charge and session methods merged, bringing the spec repository to 11 method ids.
draft-httpauth-payment-01 posted; it is a new revision, not a rename. The old draft name expired on 2026-09-18.
The pull request for a generic session intent closed without merging; session stays defined per method.
